==Background==

Pego power station was a two-unit coal-fired power plant with a total capacity of 628 MW. The plant was completed between 1992 and 1995, and was owned by [[Engie]] and [[Endesa]]. Coal was imported by CarboPego via the Port of Sines 290 km away and delivered by rail.<ref>[http://globalenergyobservatory.org/geoid/43560 "Pego Coal Power Plant Portugal,"] GEO, accessed April 2016</ref> 

In October 2019, the government announced Pego would be closed by the end of 2021.<ref>[https://www.publico.pt/2019/10/26/economia/noticia/zero-congratulase-antecipacao-fecho-centrais-carvao-pego-sines-1891491 "Zero satisfeita com antecipação do fecho das centrais a carvão do Pego e Sines,"] Publico, October 26, 2019</ref> The plant closed in late November, 2021.<ref>[https://www.reuters.com/business/cop/portugals-power-production-goes-coal-free-long-before-deadline-2021-11-22/ "Portugal's power production goes coal-free long before deadline,"] Reuters, November 23, 2021</ref><ref>[https://www.publico.pt/2021/11/21/economia/noticia/acabou-producao-electricidade-partir-carvao-portugal-1985803 "Acabou a produção de electricidade a partir do carvão em Portugal,"] Publico, November 21, 2021</ref>

In addition, the [[Sines power station]], which was originally slated to close by September 2023, was retired in January 2021.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.euractiv.com/section/energy/news/portugal-on-track-to-become-coal-free-by-year-end/|title=Portugal on track to become coal-free by year end|date=2021-01-15|work=www.euractiv.com|access-date=2021-06-22|language=en-GB}}</ref> 

There are now no operating coal-fired power plants in Portugal.
